subject: Unexpected invoice delta — session concurrency attribution question
messages:
From: Rajesh Agarwal <rajesh@novum.ai>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: billing@novum.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected invoice delta — July invoice looks 42% higher than expected

Olga,

We just received July's invoice and the total token-based charges are ~42% higher than the forecast we agreed during our Q2 review. The top-line usage pattern (per our internal dashboards) didn't change materially — same traffic, same peak concurrency — so this jump is surprising.

I've attached a small sample export (novum_sample_usage_export.csv) showing calls on 2027-07-18 and 2027-07-19 where our contract estimate and your billed token counts diverge dramatically. The billing line items show many short, overlapping sessions that appear to have been counted twice. Can you confirm whether anything changed on Redwood's side that could explain duplicate attribution or a concurrency reclassification?

We need the team to review and provide either: (a) evidence the usage is correct, or (b) an explanation and proposed credit if the billing overcounts. We are in the middle of our monthly close and the variance is material.

Thanks,
Rajesh Agarwal
Head of Platform — Novum.ai

Rajesh — I pulled the ingestion and attribution traces for 2027-07-18 00:00 to 2027-07-19 23:59 UTC against Novum.ai's account keys. Two things to call out: 

1) On 2027-07-18 ~03:00 UTC we rolled a small streaming telemetry change that altered a prefix hashing step used by an internal session coalescer. The change was intended to reduce false session merges (it tightened the hash window) but in a small subset of callers it produced non-unique prefix tokens which caused what looks like parallel session attribution for a short period (~2h).

2) Around the same period there were several clients (including Novum) using short-lived multiplexed connections where our request router produced multiple logical sessions for a single client connection. The tightened hash + multiplex pattern resulted in several transient requests being credited as separate sessions and therefore counted more tokens against the per-request metering logic.

Evidence: attached telemetry_prefix_hashes.txt (a sanitized extract) and internal usage traces (we've posted the full export to the shared Drive link in the metadata). From a counts perspective, the window produced an incremental ~38% bump in billed tokens for the affected calls. Outside that ~2h window counts look aligned.

Proposed remediation:
- We'll backfill corrected attribution for the impacted window and re-run invoicing for those line items.
- Marissa will prepare a provisional credit equal to the overage for July's invoice attributable to the double-counting window.
- Ops will revert the prefix-hash tightening change in the next maintenance window and add a canary to prevent recurrence.

Can you confirm the sample rows you sent are within the 03:00–05:00 UTC window? If yes, we'll prioritize the backfill and aim to issue a credit memo within 5 business days.

Thanks — apologies for the noise; we’ll own the corrective action.

Best,
Ben Carter
Billing Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
